summary: Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1984–1993). He held posts at Tottori University (~1998–2002) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, where he became a professor around 2009.

Shinjo Hinonishi (1924–2016) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history and archaeology who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held positions at Koyasan University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and others, as well as under Dale Riepe. He held posts at the University at Buffalo (~1964–1967) and Toyo Bunko (~1962–1975).

Shinjo Suguro (1925–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his degrees, including a Doctor of Letters (1987), from the University of Tokyo, and served at Rissho University, where he was vice director (1980) and professor emeritus (~1996–2004).

Shinjosei Mochizuki (1899–1990) specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1920–1924) and Kyoto University, and later held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1966–1978).
Shinkai Sugawara (1924–2016) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and Taisho University, and served as professor emeritus at Waseda University until 1972.

Shinkan Murakami (born 1932) is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He studied at Tohoku University under Nobuo Kumagai, Ensho Kanakura, Ryūjō Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano, later serving there as professor (~1977–1995) before joining Seiwa Gakuen College (~1995–2003).

Shinko Nakai (1943–2024) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962–1966) and served at Bukkyo University (~1977–2014) as president and professor emeritus.

Shinkō Mochizuki (1869–1948) studied under Tokuo Jonobe, at Bukkyo University, Jōdo Shūgaku Honkō, and the University of Tokyo. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928), held multiple posts at Taisho University (~1926–1942), and joined the Imperial Academy in 1947.
Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under Mark Csikszentmihalyi, Robert Bickner, and Charles Hallisey, who served as her doctoral supervisor.
Shinobu Yamaguchi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning a PhD from Nagoya University in 1995, Yamaguchi held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Toyo University (~1926–1936) and Kokugakuin University, and taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo (~1936–1959).

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda. Kitano was a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai (1912–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. Mano served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015–2019) and as a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and earned a Dr.Phil from the University of Vienna (~2000–2006), later holding a post at Shinshu University (~2008).

Shiro Matsumoto (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Waseda, Komazawa, and Tokyo universities under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi, and served as professor at Komazawa University (1995–2020), with visiting positions at Vienna and Chicago.

Shiv Nath Sharma specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir (attested 1947) and as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

Shivram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard University, Shankashastri Marulkar, and Maheshwarshastri Joshi. He served as professor and director at Savitribai Phule Pune University and at Deccan College (~1987–1996).

Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, Bukkyo University, and under Jikido Takasaki. Since 1990 he has held posts at Hanazono University, becoming Professor of Indian Buddhism in 2002.
